title: Cross-Environment Role Onboarding and Log Schema QuickRef
content:
Purpose:
This quick reference provides a compact, practical set of artifacts for onboarding roles across Redwood Inference environments (hosted, dedicated, private), with an emphasis on: (1) a minimal role onboarding matrix tuned for RBAC v2, (2) a concise SIEM export / audit-log schema required for evidence automation, and (3) patterns for ephemeral credentials and activation evidence so teams can implement automated attestations quickly.

Scope and assumptions:
- Audience: SREs, security engineers, platform onboarding owners, and compliance reviewers.
- Applies to: control-plane and compute-plane operations related to model serving, telemetry, and customer data access.
- Assumes RBAC v2 core primitives: role, permission, grant, scope (tenant, workspace, nodepool), and activation record.
- This doc is deliberately prescriptive and not exhaustive — intended as a quick operational reference to implement automation and templates.

1) Role onboarding matrix (compact)
Format: Role name | Typical owner/team | Allowed environments | Privilege scope | Activation model | Required evidence artifacts
- Role: model-ops-reader | Owner: platform-engineering | Envs: hosted,dedicated,private | Scope: tenant-read, model-metadata | Activation: static service grant | Evidence: grant record, owner email
- Role: model-ops-deployer | Owner: platform-engineering | Envs: dedicated,private | Scope: deploy:create,deploy:update,artifact-read | Activation: time-bound delegated token (1h) | Evidence: delegation request id, approver, TTL
- Role: infra-admin | Owner: infra | Envs: dedicated,private | Scope: infra:manage, network:config | Activation: privileged session (MFA + JAAS) | Evidence: session id, MFA challenge id, justification text
- Role: support-cs-analyst | Owner: customer-success | Envs: hosted | Scope: tenant-support-lookup (read-only customer metadata) | Activation: portal-approval (ticket) | Evidence: ticket-id, csr-dropdown selection
- Role: billing-auditor | Owner: finance | Envs: hosted,dedicated | Scope: billing:read, invoices:list | Activation: background scheduled token | Evidence: cron-run-id, access window

Onboarding checklist (per role):
- Create role (RBAC v2) and link to team owner in catalog.
- Define allowed environment flags: hosted/dedicated/private.
- Choose default activation model and TTL.
- Add SIEM export mapping tags (log_context.role=<role-name>).
- Create onboarding ticket and attach policy snippets + evidence retention policy.

2) Example policy templates (snippets for inclusion in onboarding docs)
- Minimal tenant-read policy (text):
  "Policy: TenantRead"
  "Description: Read-only access to tenant metadata and model catalog entries"
  "AllowedActions: [tenant:get, model:query, model:versions:list]"
  "DeniedActions: [model:deploy, infra:*]"
  "Scope: ${tenant_id}"
  "Notes: attach to role: model-ops-reader. TTL: none for service principals."

- Scoped deployer with explicit allow list (text):
  "Policy: ScopedDeployer"
  "AllowedActions: [deploy:create, deploy:update, artifacts:read]"
  "ResourceConstraints: [resource.tag(team)==${team_tag}, resource.env in (dedicated,private)]"
  "Activation: requires delegation request and approver id"

3) SIEM / audit log schema (required fields for evidence automation)
Guiding principle: every access event that can change state or grant access MUST include the fields below. Use these fields in exported JSON lines to SIEM.
- schema_version: string (e.g., v1)
- event_id: uuid
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- actor_id: user/service principal id (email or svc-UUID)
- actor_type: user | service | delegated | system
- actor_role: canonical role name(s) at time of action
- action: canonical action string (e.g., deploy.create, iam.grant, credential.rotate)
- resource_type: model|tenant|cluster|nodepool|policy
- resource_id: canonical resource identifier
- env: hosted|dedicated|private
- outcome: success|failure|partial
- auth_chain: list of principals and delegation steps (comma-separated values okay for flat schema)
- activation_id: id tying this event to an activation session (if applicable)
- evidence_refs: comma-separated evidence ids (ticket-123, mfa-789)
- ip_address: source ip if available
- user_agent: raw user agent
- request_payload_summary: short summary or hash of request body
- response_summary: short summary or hash of response body
- retention_class: e.g., compliance-7y, standard-90d (policy tag)

Notes on auth_chain: keep as a delimited string such as "user:alice->delegation:ticket-456->service:deployer-123" for compatibility with legacy SIEM ingestion.

4) Evidence automation mapping (how to assemble the record for an attestation)
Minimal attestation record (fields expected by evidence-pipeline):
- attestation_id: uuid
- linked_event_ids: comma-separated event_id(s)
- requester_id: actor_id who requested activation
- approver_id: actor_id who approved (if manual)
- justification: short free text (max 2k chars)
- artifacts: comma-separated artifact identifiers (ticket, commit-sha, approval-email-id)
- start_ts / end_ts: ISO windows for the activation
- generated_by: automation-job-id or human
- hash_of_request: sha256 of canonical request summary (for tamper detection)

Automation rules (recommended):
- If activation model == "delegated token", require linked_event_ids to include iam.grant and delegation.request events.
- If role is infra-admin, require approver_id and justification > 200 chars and attached change-request id.
- All activations that touch private deployments must have retention_class=compliance-7y and be forwarded to long-term evidence bucket.

5) Pattern: ephemeral credentials and TTLs (prescriptive defaults)
- service-to-service (machine agents): default TTL 12h; rotation automated; evidence: rotation job id.
- delegated human short-lived token (CI/CD, deployer): default TTL 1h; require delegation ticket id; evidence: ticket + approver.
- privileged interactive session (console access to infra): session TTL 15m with step-up MFA; evidence: session id, mfa-challenge id.
- long-lived service keys (only for legacy connectors): disallowed for private environments unless approved by security council; if approved, rotate every 30d and tag with approval id.

6) Environment-specific implementation notes
- Hosted: centralized SIEM ingestion (ELK stack) receives all audit events; RBAC policy enforcement is centralized in control plane. For hosted, prefer role-scoping to tenant-id only. Evidence forwarding: to central long-term bucket when retention_class=compliance-7y.
- Dedicated: mix of centralized control-plane logs + per-customer telemetry exported via per-customer SIEM connectors. When onboarding a dedicated instance, add mapping rule to add "env=dedicated, cluster_id=<cluster>" to every log line. Delegated tokens must include cluster claim.
- Private: local control plane with optional air-gapped evidence export. Private deployments must include a scheduled evidence-export job that signs and bundles attestations for periodic export (SFTP or signed artifact). Activation records must be locally retained for the compliance retention period and a hashed manifest sent to the central compliance index (small footprint).

7) Quick implementation checklist for automation engineers
- Wire schema_version and event_id generation into auth middleware.
- Standardize "actor_role" mapping in the identity service; emit canonical role names.
- Emit auth_chain for delegations.
- Ensure SIEM exporter tags each record with "env" and "retention_class".
- Implement an evidence-collector microservice that aggregates linked_event_ids into attestation records and signs them with a platform key.
- Add unit tests that verify evidence_refs cannot be empty for any iam.grant or deploy.create events.

8) Common questions and answers (short)
- Q: Can we reuse hosted role definitions for private?
  A: Yes, canonical roles should be re-used, but private deployments must add local constraints and require local evidence export.
- Q: What if a delegated approver is unavailable?
  A: Use a defined on-call bypass flow: temporary emergency approver rota. All emergency activations must be post-facto attested and flagged as emergency.

9) Appendix: example SIEM JSON line (single-line compact example)
{"schema_version":"v1","event_id":"8a7f3e4d-2c9b-4a1d-9f2b-1a2b3c4d5e6f","timestamp":"2024-11-12T14:22:31Z","actor_id":"alice@redwood.ai","actor_type":"user","actor_role":"model-ops-deployer","action":"deploy.create","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"model:tenant-42:recommendation-v3","env":"dedicated","outcome":"success","auth_chain":"user:alice->delegation:ticket-9123->service:deployer-7","activation_id":"act-3456","evidence_refs":"ticket-9123,mfa-204","ip_address":"203.0.113.17","user_agent":"redwood-cli/1.4","request_payload_summary":"sha256:abcd...","response_summary":"ok:deploy-started","retention_class":"compliance-7y"}

10) Next steps and owners
- Platform engineering: implement actor_role canonicalization and schema hooks (owner: Marcus Patel).
- SRE: add env tagging for dedicated clusters and private export hook (owner: Leah Ortiz).
- Security: finalize automated attestation contract and signing key rotation cadence (owner: Avery Chen).

If any team wants this turned into a templated onboarding ticket + IaC snippet for enforcement, ping the doc owners and we will convert the quickref into a slot-based template.

End of quickref.
